article.title: Find a message in the log
article.excerpt: The log answers "what happened to this one message" — without storing anyone's content.

p: The log is built for operations and reconciliation, which is why it keeps metadata rather than traffic.
list: Time, destination number, tenant, provider, sender, normalized status, provider message ID and raw error code.
The batch or campaign a message belonged to, when there was one.
sections.scope: Message bodies are never persisted — for compliance, and because the platform does not need them to deliver. Retention is plan-based: 7 days on Free and Growth, 30 on Pro, 90 on Ultra. Past that window records are deleted by a TTL index, so export anything you must keep.

steps.p: Start with the window around the send, then add the recipient number.
This is the fastest way to isolate a single conversation, including its duplicates.
Use the status filter to separate suppressed from failed, and the provider filter to see whether one channel is behaving differently.
The detail view shows the full status history, raw provider wording and the error code, if any.

p: A comparison card aggregates your own channels side by side — submit success rate, delivery rate and latency. It is the quickest way to see that one provider account is underperforming before it shows up in customer complaints.
Exports run asynchronously and are truncated at 1,000,000 rows. A truncated export is reported as truncated rather than silently shortened, so check that flag before treating a file as complete.
